items.stem: Which of the following statements about circles is NOT correct?
items.answer: The radius of x² + y² = 16 is 16.
items.markingKey: (d) "The radius of x² + y² = 16 is 16." is false; the other three are true.
options: x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has centre (−g, −f).
A circle is a conic obtained when the plane is perpendicular to the axis of the cone.
The radius of x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 is √(g² + f² − c).
The radius of x² + y² = 16 is 16.

items.stem: Name the four conic sections and say how each arises from a double cone.
items.answer: Circle (β = 90°), ellipse (α < β < 90°), parabola (β = α), hyperbola (0 ≤ β < α).
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): x² + y² + 2x + 2y + 5 = 0 represents a real circle.
Reason (R): For x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 the radius is √(g² + f² − c).
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: g² + f² − c = −3 < 0; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Find the centre and the radius of the circle x² + y² − 2x − 10y + 10 = 0.
items.markingKey: complete the squares: (x − 1)² + (y − 5)² = 16 (1) ⇒ centre (1, 5), radius √16 = 4 (1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the circle with the ends of a diameter at (−3, −4) and (1, 6).
The point (8, 4) lies, with respect to the circle x² + y² + 4x + 2y − 20 = 0,
items.markingKey: (a) Centre (−2, −1), r² = 25; the square of the distance of the point from the centre is 125, so it is outside the circle.
options: outside the circle
on the circle
inside the circle
at the centre

items.stem: Derive the equation of a circle with centre (h, k) and radius r.
items.answer: A point P(x, y) lies on it iff the distance CP = r ⇒ (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0 is a circle of radius 5.
Reason (R): Completing squares gives (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Find the equation of the circle with centre (4, 0) and radius 4.
items.markingKey: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²: (x − (4))² + (y − (0))² = 16; expanding gives x² + y² − 8x = 0.

items.stem: Find the equation of the circle passing through (−7, 0) and (−7, 8) whose centre lies on the line y = −x + 4.
items.markingKey: Let the centre be (h, −1h + 4) (1); equate distances to the two points (2) ⇒ h = 0, centre (0, 4) (1); r² = 65: x² + y² − 8y − 49 = 0 (1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the circle passing through (0, 0), (−5, 0) and (0, 5).
items.markingKey: Substitute the three points in x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 (1): c = 0 (1), g = 5/2, f = −5/2 (2); equation x² + y² + 5x − 5y = 0 (1).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The circle x² + y² = 25 passes through (3, 4).
Reason (R): 3² + 4² = 25.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Find the centre and the radius of the circle x² + y² − 10x + 10y + 25 = 0.
items.markingKey: complete the squares: (x − 5)² + (y − (−5))² = 25 (1) ⇒ centre (5, −5), radius √25 = 5 (1).

items.stem: When a double cone (semi-vertical angle α) is cut by a plane making angle β with the axis, a parabola is obtained when
items.answer: β = α, the plane is parallel to a generator
items.markingKey: (a) parabola: β = α, the plane is parallel to a generator.
options: β = α, the plane is parallel to a generator
α < β < 90°, the plane cuts only one nappe across
the cutting plane is perpendicular to the axis of the cone (β = 90°)
0 ≤ β < α, the plane cuts both nappes

items.stem: Find the equation of the circle passing through (−12, 2) and (−11, −3) whose centre lies on the line y = x + 5.
items.markingKey: Let the centre be (h, 1h + 5) (1); equate distances to the two points (2) ⇒ h = −4, centre (−4, 1) (1); r² = 65: x² + y² + 8x − 2y − 48 = 0 (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about parabolas is correct?
items.answer: A parabola is the set of points equidistant from a fixed point (focus) and a fixed line (directrix).
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: "A parabola is the set of points equidistant from a fixed point (focus) and a fixed line (directrix)." The other three are false.
options: A parabola is the set of points equidistant from a fixed point (focus) and a fixed line (directrix).
The latus rectum of y² = 12x has length 3.
For y² = 4ax, the directrix is x = a.
x² = 4ay is symmetric about the x-axis.

items.stem: Explain why a parabolic reflector is used in car headlights.
items.answer: Light from a source at the focus reflects off the parabola into a beam parallel to the axis.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem:

items.stem: For the parabola y² = 5x, find the length of the latus rectum and the axis of the parabola.
items.markingKey: a = 5/4; latus rectum = 4a = 5 (1); the parabola is symmetric about y = 0 (the x-axis) (1).

items.stem:
A dish antenna on a rooftop in Coimbatore has a parabolic cross-section. The dish is 16 dm across at the rim and 5 dm deep. Take the vertex at the origin and the axis along the positive y-axis.
(i) Write the form of the equation of the parabola. (ii) Find its equation. (iii) Where should the receiver be placed (focus)? (iv) Find the depth of the dish at 2 dm from the axis.
items.answer: (i) x² = 4ay (ii) 5x² = 64y (iii) at (0, 16/5) dm, i.e. 16/5 dm above the vertex (iv) 5/16 dm
items.markingKey: (i) Opens upward (1). (ii) Rim point (8, 5) on it (1). (iii) Focus (0, a) (1). (iv) put x = 2 in 5x² = 64y (1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the parabola with vertex (0, 0) and focus (0, 5/4).
items.markingKey: The focus lies on the y-axis, opening up (1); a = 5/4 and the form is x² = 4ay (1): x² = 5y (1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the parabola with vertex at the origin, symmetric about the y-axis and passing through (−6, −5).
items.markingKey: Form x² = ky (1); substitute (−6, −5): k = −36/5 (1); equation 5x² = −36y (1).

items.stem: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in the parabola y² = 16x with one vertex at the vertex of the parabola. Find the length of its side.
items.markingKey: Let the other vertices be (h, ±k) by symmetry (1); for 60° at the vertex, k/h = tan 30° = 1/√3 (1); k² = 16h gives h = 48, k = 16√3 (2); side = 2k = 32√3 (1).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The parabola x² = −16y opens downward.
Reason (R): For x² = −4ay with a > 0, y must be ≤ 0.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the focus and the equation of the directrix of the parabola y² = −8x.
items.markingKey: Compare with y² = −4ax: a = 2 (1); focus (−2, 0), directrix x = 2 (1).

items.stem: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in the parabola y² = 4x with one vertex at the vertex of the parabola. Find the length of its side.
items.markingKey: Let the other vertices be (h, ±k) by symmetry (1); for 60° at the vertex, k/h = tan 30° = 1/√3 (1); k² = 4h gives h = 12, k = 4√3 (2); side = 2k = 8√3 (1).

items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (x = −2); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.markingKey: a = 1/2; latus rectum = 4a = 2 (1); the parabola is symmetric about y = 0 (the x-axis) (1).

items.stem: For the parabola x² = −20y, find the length of the latus rectum and the axis of the parabola.
items.markingKey: a = 5; latus rectum = 4a = 20 (1); the parabola is symmetric about x = 0 (the y-axis) (1).

items.stem:

items.stem: Find the equation of the parabola with focus (0, 1/2) and directrix y = −1/2.
items.markingKey: The focus lies on the y-axis, opening up (1); a = 1/2 and the form is x² = 4ay (1): x² = 2y (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ellipses is correct?
items.answer: A circle is an ellipse with e = 0.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: "A circle is an ellipse with e = 0." The other three are false.

The eccentricity of an ellipse is greater than 1.

items.stem: Explain why the eccentricity of an ellipse lies between 0 and 1.
items.answer: e = c/a with 0 ≤ c < a; e = 0 gives a circle, e close to 1 a flat ellipse.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Find the equation of the ellipse, with centre at the origin and axes along the coordinate axes, which passes through (4, 3) and (6, 2).
items.markingKey: Let x²/A + y²/B = 1 (1); substitute both points to get two linear equations in 1/A and 1/B (2); solve: A = 52, B = 13 (1); x²/52 + y²/13 = 1 (1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the ellipse, with centre at the origin and axes along the coordinate axes, which passes through (2, 2) and (4, 1).

items.stem: Show that for an ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (a > b), the length of the latus rectum is 2b²/a.
items.answer: At x = c, y² = b²(1 − c²/a²) = b⁴/a², so y = ±b²/a; length 2b²/a.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: A rod of length 20 cm moves with its ends always on the x- and y-axes. Find the equation of the locus of the point P on the rod that is 17 cm from the end in contact with the x-axis.

items.stem:
Two radio stations S₁ and S₂ on a straight coast are 10 km apart. A ship receives their signals and finds that it is always 8 km farther from S₁ than from S₂. Take the midpoint of S₁S₂ as the origin and the coast as the x-axis.
(i) Name the curve on which the ship lies. (ii) Find a, c and b². (iii) Write the equation of the curve. (iv) Find its eccentricity.
items.answer: (i) a branch of a hyperbola with foci S₁, S₂ (ii) a = 4, c = 5, b² = 9 (iii) x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 (iv) 5/4
items.markingKey: (i) Constant difference of distances from two fixed points (1). (ii) 2a = difference, 2c = distance between foci, b² = c² − a² (1). (iii) Standard form (1). (iv) e = c/a (1).

Two radio stations S₁ and S₂ on a straight coast are 26 km apart. A ship receives their signals and finds that it is always 10 km farther from S₁ than from S₂. Take the midpoint of S₁S₂ as the origin and the coast as the x-axis.
(i) Name the curve on which the ship lies. (ii) Find a, c and b². (iii) Write the equation of the curve. (iv) Find its eccentricity.
items.answer: (i) a branch of a hyperbola with foci S₁, S₂ (ii) a = 5, c = 13, b² = 144 (iii) x²/25 − y²/144 = 1 (iv) 13/5
items.markingKey: (i) Constant difference of distances from two fixed points (1). (ii) 2a = difference, 2c = distance between foci, b² = c² − a² (1). (iii) Standard form (1). (iv) e = c/a (1).

items.stem: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in the parabola y² = 12x with one vertex at the vertex of the parabola. Find the length of its side.
